jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in mineral resources - DTU Sustain
jobs.description:
If you are establishing your career as scientist and you are looking for the best possible foundation for fulfilling your ambitions, it is right here in front of you. At DTU Sustain, you will break new ground by entering an interdisciplinary and international collaboration focusing on critical raw materials.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The position is one of two interdependent PhD projects hosted by DTU Sustain and University of Queensland (UQ), respectively. The applicant will receive joint supervision from the two hosts and is expected to spend a total of six months during the project at UQ (Australia), and to engage in collaboration with the UQ-hosted PhD project. 

The overall aim of the project is to create synergy between in depth mineral characterization and thermodynamic stabilities (DTU-lead), and its correlation with the propensity for microbially-mediated metal dissolution by nature-based mineral-based microbial consortia for metal recovery (UQ-lead) to create a fundamentals-to-application pipeline for sustainable metal recovery. The candidate will be responsible for conducting research on thermodynamic properties of minerals that are potential ores for critical raw materials. This will be done from first principle using, e.g., density functional theory. Other tasks will include teaching and possibly co-supervision of MSc and BSc students.

The candidate is expected to have a scientific background that enables independent research into thermodynamic systems using first principles. These qualifications must be demonstrated in the application. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree in geology, mineralogy, geoscience, physics, chemistry, crystallography or similar.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Electrolyte Solvation and Interphase Engineering for Rechargeable Calcium Batteries
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from 1st of March 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks
You will develop and investigate non-aqueous liquid electrolytes for rechargeable calcium batteries, focusing on how Ca2+ solvation, ion pairing and interphase formation govern electrochemical reversibility. Your work will contribute to a complementary research programme on calcium-battery electrode materials and cell development at AAU Energy.

You will systematically vary salt chemistry, solvent composition and concentration within selected electrolyte families. Physicochemical measurements and spectroscopic analysis will be used to examine electrolyte coordination environments and ion association. These investigations will guide the selection of formulations for detailed electrochemical and interfacial studies.

A central part of the work will be the design and evaluation of calcium plating and stripping experiments, including measurements of coulombic efficiency, polarization and cycling stability under defined conditions. You will use appropriate controls and complementary analyses to verify metallic calcium deposition and distinguish it from electrolyte decomposition or other electrochemical reactions. You will investigate electrode interphase composition and evolution using XPS, supported by electron microscopy and, where appropriate, ToF-SIMS for morphology and species distribution. Raman spectroscopy, complemented by NMR where relevant, will probe electrolyte coordination and ion association. Targeted MD simulations may clarify Ca²⁺ solvation and ion pairing. Correlating these findings with electrochemical performance will establish mechanism-based guidelines for electrolyte formulation and selection.

Working closely with the PhD researcher developing cathode and calcium-alloying anode materials, you will assess selected electrode–electrolyte combinations and contribute to reproducible coin-cell evaluation. You will also contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, teaching, supervision of student projects and departmental dissemination activities.

The position is offered in relation to the Batteries research group, and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Power Electronics Systems Integration and Materials”.

Your competencies 
Applicants are expected to hold an M.Sc. degree in chemistry, materials science, physics, chemical engineering, or a closely related discipline. Candidates should have a solid scientific background and preferably hands-on experience in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, electrolyte formulation and preparation, battery testing and characterization, or the handling of air- and moisture-sensitive materials under controlled environments. A strong interest in electrochemical energy storage, interfacial chemistry, spectroscopic characterization techniques, and quantitative experimental data analysis is highly desirable.

Experience with advanced characterization techniques, particularly spectroscopy and surface analysis, will be considered an advantage. Familiarity with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations or other computational approaches for investigating electrolyte properties is beneficial but not essential, as the position is primarily focused on experimental research.

Excellent written and spoken English communication skills, together with the ability to collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary and international research environment, are essential.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real world energy challenges.

Aalborg University has been ranked as the best university in Europe within energy research and is among the very best universities worldwide in this field. At AAU Energy you will be part of a top international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges such as the green transition and future energy systems.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and with diverse national and disciplinary backgrounds, which creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as working language in both research and teaching, which supports the integration of international colleagues.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Project description (2-5 pages), that describes the applicant’s initial thoughts and ideas related to the specific project applied for. This includes a brief state-of-the-art (including short list of references), a time schedule and how the applicant intends to shed light on the project objectives.
• Other relevant documents
The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost. 

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

**You Have

**

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

**In Practice, You Will

**

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. The role has no direct reports, but you will lead through influence: category groups and project teams with specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Finance and Legal, as well as colleagues in Global Contract Manufacturing DS, Supply Chain Design, GMS Management and country affiliates.

Externally, you will work with CMOs across the US, Europe and Asia, so you should expect to spend significant time abroad. You will balance partnership and long-term collaboration with the best possible commercial terms for Novo, and you will be at ease handling cross-cultural discussions when tension runs high.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. Your primary focus will be Drug Substance, with potential involvement in Drug Product and Devices.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

You will also have room to challenge convention: to find faster, better ways to run projects and to shape new processes and standards for CMO partnerships.

The pay range for this role is 940,800 – 1,448,700 DKK per year. The final offer reflects your experience and qualifications.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Novo’s most strategic CMO partnerships from strategy to signature, apply for the Project Director role by 19st November 2026 . We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.
